articles.title: What one generated image costs, and why my account total did not show it
articles.excerpt: What one generated image costs, and why my account total did not show it I generate artwork for a few channels through a hosted image model, one call per piece, from a script. For about a month every…
articles.body: What one generated image costs, and why my account total did not show it I generate artwork for a few channels through a hosted image model, one call per piece, from a script. For about a month every call came back HTTP 402 with the same body: This account never purchased credits . The key had been on disk the whole time, and the same key answered a read on the account endpoint without complaint. A 402 is a billing state, not a bad key The two status codes get lumped together when a request fails and nobody stops to read the body. 401 means the request did not carry credentials the server accepts. 402 means the credentials were accepted and the account behind them has no balance to spend.

articles.title: How to keep signed license keys short
articles.excerpt: A fully-formed license key is a signed document. It carries a licensee, a tier, an expiry, a machine binding and a list of entitlements, and it is signed so a client can trust it offline. The trouble…
articles.body: A fully-formed license key is a signed document. It carries a licensee, a tier, an expiry, a machine binding and a list of entitlements, and it is signed so a client can trust it offline. The trouble is that all of that adds up. An Ed25519 signature is a fixed 64 bytes. A compact entitlement payload is easily 200–400 bytes more. Base64 the concatenation and you hand the customer a 500-character string to paste into a dialog box. People mistype it, email clients wrap it, and support tickets pile up. The instinct is to compress the payload. The instinct is right — but the obvious way to do it is a trap that silently breaks verification on a subset of machines. The ordering that fails The tempting pipeline is compress, then sign the compressed bytes .

articles.body: Windows 11 removed classic taskbar network speed toolbars—and most third-party monitors are heavy Electron apps or packed with ads. So I built NetSpeedMeter , an open-source (MIT), zero-dependency Windows 10 & 11 utility compiled with Windows' built-in .NET Framework 4.x ( csc.exe ) that weighs ~58 KB . Key Features Live Download & Upload Speeds: Color-coded ( Cyan download, Amber upload) right beside your system tray. Per-Monitor High-DPI Scaling: Scales cleanly on 100%, 125%, 150%, and 200% laptop displays ( GetDpiForWindow + WM_DPICHANGED ). Two Layouts: Two-Line Stacked (compact) or Single-Line Horizontal. Sleep/Wake Spike Guard: Prevents bogus bandwidth spikes when laptops resume from sleep or hibernation.

articles.title: Zero Backlog: A Canary in the Mine
articles.excerpt: What happens when AI coding agents meet a way of working designed to use them? In my last article, I wrote about a Harvard study showing that many organizations are using AI to write more code without…
articles.body: What happens when AI coding agents meet a way of working designed to use them? In my last article, I wrote about a Harvard study showing that many organizations are using AI to write more code without delivering more software . The problem wasn't that AI couldn't produce code. It was that the code got stuck in the rest of the system: review, testing, approval, and coordination. I argued that the answer isn't just to add agents. It's to change how work flows through an organization. Here is what that can look like in practice: we started the project with 67 issues in the backlog. We are going into the Christmas holidays with zero. Zero backlog is a signal, not a goal Zero backlog shouldn't be a target.

articles.title: SpaceX Starship debris becomes art in Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' (video, photos)
articles.excerpt: Explore Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' Monuments in marble, Ejecta prints, Launch Sequence sculptures and interactive Crowded Sky at Heft Gallery in New York City.
articles.body: When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Some of that material now hangs on a gallery wall in New York City, embedded in artist Ashley Zelinskie's print of the very explosion it survived. Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. "I think you might want these," Zelinskie recalled one friend telling her. She did. The Brooklyn-based artist ground the fragments into dust and worked them into the print. Ashley Zelinskie incorporated dust from recovered SpaceX Starship heat-shield tiles into this print of the vehicle breaking apart over Turks and Caicos.

The most obvious change in this depressing dystopia is that replicants are running the LA show after some unmentionable ecological disaster and humans are now the ones relegated to underclass citizens. Starring Michelle Yeoh as a replicant cop named Olwen whose life clock is running out and Hunter Schafer as Cora, a desperate human posing as a replicant blade runner, "Blade Runner 2099" unties these two in a mystery revolving around a rogue blade runner and a deadly secret that might cause their city to implode.

articles.title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus
articles.excerpt: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can he…
articles.body: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving. Strawberries grown in the Space Life Sciences Lab’s controlled environment chamber. Cucumbers are grown in a controlled environment chamber at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Lemon basil is growing in chambers on the International Space Station. NASA Recent testing points to strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil as potential options for future explorers. Space crops can absorb carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, and recycle water.

articles.excerpt: In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative. With several ot…
articles.body: In an announcement on Wednesday , the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative . With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space , including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full "constellation" of AI satellites. The FCC's approval requires SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033, and meet the 1 million satellite milestone by 2040.
